The multi-agent platform deploys as a Kubernetes-native Helm chart inside the customer's own perimeter and correlates Kubernetes, observability (Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch), cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), CI/CD, and ticketing data to produce evidence-backed root cause analysis, autonomous incident response, and scheduled operations work such as CVE blast-radius mapping, RBAC drift audits, cluster right-sizing, and cost triage. It runs read-only by default, is bring-your-own-model (Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama), and keeps all data in-cluster with no external egress, targeting GDPR, BaFin, DORA, and NIS2 compliance requirements. Backed by partech; raised a EUR 3M pre-seed round.

providers.name: Sardine
providers.description: Sardine is a San Francisco-based fraud prevention, AML compliance, and risk management platform for fintechs, banks, marketplaces, and crypto VASPs. It unifies onboarding (KYC, KYB, document and bank verification), device intelligence and behavioral biometrics, payment and card fraud scoring, AML transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and case management into a single risk operating system. Sardine's "agentic" layer applies atomic agents (OSINT, data analysis, transaction monitoring, business due diligence, sanctions screening) to compress investigation time from days to minutes, while Sonar provides cross-industry fraud intelligence across the consortium. The platform serves 400+ enterprise customers including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Nubank, Novo, and bunq, has screened $1.3T+ in payments, and profiled 5.4B+ devices. Sardine has raised ~$170M from Andreessen Horowitz, Visa, Experian, Google Ventures, FIS, and others. Public docs cover the risk landscape and integration overview; full API reference, SDKs, and sandbox access are gated and require a Sardine account.

providers.name: Certinal
providers.description: Certinal provides a Healthcare Consent & Compliance Platform that digitizes consent capture, electronic signatures, and patient intake, integrating directly with EHR systems such as Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, and OpenEMR. The platform is designed for healthcare organizations to meet regulatory requirements including HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11, CMS‑0053‑F, DPDP, and PDPA, and to automate consent workflows across surgical, clinical trial, telehealth, and general treatment contexts.

providers.name: Velocity Global
providers.description: Velocity Global (now Pebl) is a global employment and Employer of Record (EOR) platform with REST APIs for international hiring, managing employee records, payroll processing, and compliance management across 185+ countries. The platform enables organizations to onboard global employees, process payroll, administer benefits, and maintain local labor law compliance without establishing local entities.

providers.name: Levelpath
providers.description: Levelpath is an AI-native procurement platform that unifies intake and orchestration, strategic sourcing, contract lifecycle management, supplier management, third-party risk management, invoice automation, and category pipeline reporting into a single enterprise system. The product is built around AI agents that run sourcing events and generate RFPs, scan contract repositories to answer questions and flag risk, monitor supplier compliance signals, and process invoices. Levelpath is a closed enterprise platform: it operates customer and supplier applications at app.levelpath.com and supplierhub.levelpath.com, and its status page confirms a production APIs component, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. Integrations with SAP, Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, NetSuite, Docusign, Ironclad, OneTrust, Slack, and Microsoft Teams are delivered through the platform rather than a documented public API. Backed by Battery Ventures, Menlo Ventures, and Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Knox Systems
providers.description: Knox Systems is a federal cloud compliance and managed-security company that provides an accelerated path to FedRAMP authorization for SaaS and AI vendors selling into the U.S. government, marketed as "FedRAMP in 90 days for 90% less." Its platform combines a pre-authorized FedRAMP boundary, a deployable Landing Zone, hardened images, and Knox AI — a continuous-monitoring and automated remediation engine trained on federal audit data — running across AWS, Azure, and GCP at FedRAMP Moderate, FedRAMP High, and DISA Impact Level 4. Vendors inherit Knox's authorization and controls rather than pursuing an independent ATO, and Knox reports 15+ authorizations to operate across federal and DoD agencies including DHS, FEMA, the Marine Corps, Treasury, and the VA. Knox Systems is a private company backed by Felicis, and operates a partner-led business rather than a public developer API program — as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Paper Instruments
providers.description: Paper Instruments provides frontier open‑source AI models for knowledge work, spanning finance, consulting, law, and operations. Their platform offers model libraries, Python SDKs, and tools that enable professionals to automate analysis, generate reports, and streamline decision‑making across multiple domains.

providers.name: Alma
providers.description: Alma is a technology-enabled U.S. immigration law firm for companies and individuals, combining licensed immigration attorneys with a platform that learns from every case it files. Alma takes end-to-end ownership of the employment-based immigration process — from initial assessment through approval — across temporary work visas (E-2, E-3, H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, O-1A, O-1B, TN) and employment-based green cards (EB-1A, EB-1B, EB-1C, EB-2 NIW, EB-2 PERM, EB-3). For employers it offers a case-management platform with real-time visibility, LCA/compliance tooling, spend forecasting, SSO, and HRIS/ATS integrations (Workday, ADP, BambooHR, UKG, and more). Alma publishes no public developer API; system integration is delivered through its enterprise plan on SOC 2 Type II infrastructure. This profile was surfaced via VC-portfolio discovery and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: General Legal
providers.description: General Legal is an AI-native law firm for high-growth startups and SMBs, offering flat-fee commercial, corporate, and employment legal work delivered by U.S.-barred attorneys augmented with proprietary AI workflows. The firm focuses on contract review, redlining, negotiation, and drafting with transparent flat pricing (from $250) and fast turnaround (median under three hours), positioning itself as "outside counsel that scales like software." Practice areas include technology transactions, employment, data privacy, financial regulatory, blockchain/cryptocurrency, and emerging companies / VC. Founded in 2026 by Ryan Walker (ex-Casetext CTO), J.P. Mohler, and Javed Qadruddin, the company is a Y Combinator (W26) portfolio company that raised $11.5M across pre-seed and seed rounds. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from public sources; General Legal is a legal-services company and does not currently publish a developer API.

providers.name: Kalderos
providers.description: Kalderos is a Chicago-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016, that built what it calls the first Drug Discount Management platform. It helps pharmaceutical manufacturers, covered entities (safety-net healthcare providers), and state Medicaid programs manage compliance across U.S. drug discount programs — most notably 340B — using data, AI, and machine learning to identify noncompliant or duplicate discounts, streamline good-faith-inquiry and dispute resolution, and move rebates transparently between stakeholders. Marquee products include 340B Pay, the Truzo rebate-payment platform, Discount Hub for covered entities, and MDRP and Commercial Discount Monitoring for manufacturers. Kalderos was acquired by Model N in 2024 to expand Model N's revenue-management and 340B capabilities for life sciences. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Kalderos operates a customer-facing application (app.kalderos.com) and previously published developer API documentation that is no longer resolvable post-acquisition.

providers.name: ZeroThreat
providers.description: ZeroThreat offers an AI‑driven automated penetration testing platform that continuously tests modern web applications and APIs. It provides end‑to‑end coverage—including authentication flows, business logic, and API attack patterns—and delivers exploit‑validated proof and audit‑ready reports for enterprise security teams, DevOps pipelines, SaaS providers, developers, MSSPs, and startups.

providers.name: Behavox
providers.description: Behavox is an AI-native compliance and conduct-surveillance software company serving the world's leading financial institutions and regulated enterprises. Its Unified AI Controls Platform spans directive, preventive, detective, and corrective controls — including Quantum (voice and text communication surveillance across 50+ languages and 150+ channels), Polaris (trade surveillance), Falcon (insider-threat and human-risk detection), Compass (conflicts of interest and personal account dealing), Atlas (control-room enforcement), Pathfinder (regulatory-change-to-policy), Intelligent Archive, Digital Employees, and Mosaic front-office revenue intelligence. Behavox is backed by Index Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company sells directly to enterprise financial-services customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Stark
providers.description: Stark is a digital accessibility compliance platform used by more than 50,000 companies as their accessibility infrastructure across the entire software product lifecycle, from issue detection and remediation to insights and governance. Stark ships design-tool plug-ins for Figma, Sketch, and Adobe XD, browser extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Arc, and Brave, a web dashboard for project management and real-time reporting, and a Compliance Center for managing accessibility posture against regulatory frameworks such as WCAG, ADA, and the European Accessibility Act. Stark does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and the security, trust, and operational-transparency surfaces it publishes.

providers.name: Avvo
providers.description: Avvo is an online legal services marketplace connecting consumers with attorneys across the United States. Founded in 2006, Avvo provides a searchable lawyer directory, free legal Q&A, client reviews, and a proprietary rating system to help users find and evaluate legal professionals. The platform also offers tools for lawyers to manage their online presence and attract clients.

providers.name: eID Easy
providers.description: eID Easy provides a cloud‑based platform for electronic signatures, e‑sealing and digital identity verification. Their API lets businesses integrate qualified electronic signatures, batch signing, one‑shot signatures, hash‑based signing, timestamping and seal creation into workflows. It also offers OAuth‑2.0 based identity‑as‑a‑service, supporting European Digital Identity Wallets and national eID systems via OpenID Connect. The service targets fintech, document management, healthcare, HR and compliance use‑cases, offering on‑premise seal options and SDKs for web and mobile integration.

providers.name: Privado
providers.description: Privado (Privado.ai) is a privacy engineering and data-privacy compliance company that helps engineering and privacy teams build privacy-first products. Its flagship is an open-source static code-analysis scanner that detects personal-data flows in source code, finds data-security violations, and generates compliance artifacts such as RoPA and Google Play Store Data Safety reports. The scanner runs locally or in CI/CD (Docker-based) via the Privado CLI, and results can optionally sync to the Privado Cloud dashboard where products like Wren (an AI privacy analyst), Agentic Assessments, Dynamic Data Maps, Web Auditor, and App Auditor automate data mapping and privacy impact assessments. Privado is a DevSecOps / privacy-governance tool rather than a public REST API provider; its developer surface is the open-source scanner, the CLI, and the docs at docs.privado.ai. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: AllWork
providers.description: AllWork is a New York-based flexible-workforce management and payments platform for contingent labor. It combines onboarding, scheduling, budgeting and planning, time and attendance with GPS-confirmed check-in, timesheet and expense approval, payroll, reporting and analytics, and a manager mobile app into one system, and acts as both Employer of Record (EOR) and Agent of Record (AOR) so a brand can compliantly engage and pay W-2 and 1099 talent across the United States, Canada and internationally. It sells into beauty and luxury, retail, food and beverage, oil and gas, technology and engineering, life sciences and healthcare, financial services, and self-direction programs, handling worker classification, labor-law adherence, and federal, state and local tax filings. AllWork publishes no public developer program: there is no API reference, no SDK, and no machine-readable specification on its site.

providers.name: Brickanta
providers.description: Brickanta is a Stockholm-based agentic AI platform built for the construction industry, deploying specialized AI agents to automate pre-construction and project workflows including bid analysis, cost estimation, procurement package generation, document and contract review, compliance, and quality assurance. The platform reads drawings, specs, and contracts to surface risks and gaps, turns raw RFPs into discipline-specific procurement packages, and builds a searchable knowledge base from every finished project. Brickanta raised an $8M seed round led by Northzone in early 2026 and serves construction teams across eleven countries. The company exposes a customer application and a public trust portal but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: NERC
providers.description: The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is the not-for-profit international regulatory authority certified by FERC in July 2006 as the Electric Reliability Organization under Section 215 of the Federal Power Act, added by the Energy Policy Act of 2005. From offices in Washington, DC and Atlanta, and working through six Regional Entities (MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, Texas RE, WECC), NERC develops and enforces the mandatory Reliability Standards, including the CIP cyber security standards, that govern the bulk power system across the contiguous United States, all of Canada, and a portion of Baja California, Mexico. It registers and certifies the entities that operate that system, monitors and enforces compliance, runs the Electricity Information Sharing and Analysis Center (E-ISAC), and collects mandatory industry performance data through Rules of Procedure Section 1600 data requests into GADS, TADS, DADS and MIDAS. NERC sits at the top of the North American bulk-power value chain, above the ISOs/RTOs, transmission owners and generator owners it registers, and entirely above the retail utility-to-customer relationship. Its API posture is the plainest in this series. NERC publishes NO developer API, NO OpenAPI, NO SDK, NO developer portal and NO open data portal. A site search of nerc.com for the term API on 2026-07-27 returned zero matching documents. NERC is a MANDATOR of energy data, not a publisher of it. The obligation it imposes is to SUBMIT data upward to NERC, and the data submitted is explicitly confidential under Rules of Procedure Section 1500. What NERC does publish anonymously is documents: reliability assessments, the State of Reliability report, aggregated GADS/TADS statistics, Power BI dashboards and the public NERC Compliance Registry Matrix spreadsheet of every registered entity. Everything machine-facing, including the ERO Portal, Align, the Secure Evidence Locker, CORES, the GADS/TADS data stores and the E-ISAC portal, is behind an approved account. No Green Button, no ESPI, no consumer data right, and no consumer usage or billing API exists anywhere in NERC's surface, because retail customer data is outside its reach entirely. NERC is a regulator whose peer FERC publishes a documented public API and whose neighbour EIA publishes one of the best government APIs anywhere, while NERC itself publishes none.

providers.name: Risk Ledger
providers.description: Risk Ledger is a London-based third-party and supply chain risk management platform that helps organizations assess, monitor, and continuously manage the security risks across their supplier networks. Through its "Active Supply Chain Security" model and a connected network of 16,000+ organizations, suppliers complete a single standardized security assessment once and share it with every client, eliminating repetitive questionnaires. The platform maps supply chains from third through sixth parties, surfaces concentration risk, and delivers emerging-threat intelligence and breach monitoring with remediation tracking. Risk Ledger serves the public sector, critical national infrastructure, financial services and insurance, and technology sectors, and is ISO/IEC 27001 and Cyber Essentials certified. It is backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: Carbide
providers.description: Carbide (carbidesecure.com) is a compliance-automation and risk-management platform that pairs software with credentialed security advisors to help fast-growing organizations achieve and maintain security certifications and regulatory compliance. The platform automates evidence collection, maps controls across frameworks, tracks remediation tasks, surfaces compliance gaps, and continuously monitors cloud and business-tool integrations. Carbide supports SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, CMMC, CPCSC, GDPR, CCPA, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, PCI DSS, PIPEDA, and custom frameworks, and offers penetration testing and a customer-facing Trust Center product. Carbide is a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: Luminos.AI
providers.description: Luminos.AI is an AI governance and evaluation platform that tests AI systems — classical machine learning, generative AI, and autonomous agents — for legal, regulatory, and reputational risk. The platform automates continuous evaluations against customizable risks, generates privileged, audit-ready compliance documentation, runs approval and governance workflows, and monitors deployed models in real time for drift, updates, and deployment-context changes, all without requiring direct access to the underlying model. Luminos.AI was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and profiled into the API Evangelist network. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition; the product is engaged through hosted evaluations and demos.

providers.name: Peony
providers.description: Peony is a virtual data room (VDR) platform for secure document sharing, page-level analytics, due diligence workflows, AI-powered Q&A, and legally binding e-signatures. Founded in 2021 by Deqian Jia and headquartered in San Francisco with a London office, Peony positions itself as a design-led, premium alternative to legacy VDR vendors such as DocSend, Datasite, Firmex, Digify, and Ideals. The platform offers NDA-gated access, dynamic viewer-identity watermarks, screenshot protection, granular permissions, custom-domain delivery, AI document extraction and redaction, and detailed audit logs. It is SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA compliant, serving 5,900+ teams including YC startups, M&A advisors, and funds managing over $19.6B in assets.

providers.name: Stilta
providers.description: Stilta is an agentic AI platform for high-stakes patent and intellectual property work, backed by a16z, NVIDIA, and Y Combinator (W26). Its agents automate evidence gathering and analysis across 180M+ patents, scientific literature, and archived web content to deliver source-cited invalidity analysis, infringement analysis, and freedom-to-operate assessments for in-house IP teams and intellectual property law firms. The platform markets a defensible first answer in roughly seventeen minutes, fully autonomous, with citations pulled from original documents. Stilta exposes a first-party backend API (api.stilta.com, "Patrona Patent Search Platform API") and a PropelAuth-based OpenID Connect identity surface at auth.stilta.com, but does not publish public developer documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as an a16z / Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from Stilta's public web surface.

providers.name: AdvisorCheck
providers.description: AdvisorCheck is a consumer-first platform for researching, comparing and continuously monitoring US financial advisors and the firms they work for. It compiles verified public regulatory data — FINRA BrokerCheck, the SEC's Investment Adviser Public Disclosure (IAPD) system, court records and six industry certification bodies — into profiles covering roughly 380,000 investment adviser representatives and 620,000 registered representatives. A free tier covers search and basic advisor monitoring; the paid AdvisorCheck Premium membership adds Advanced Monitoring with firm-stability insights (AUM changes, advisor headcount and retention, client acquisition trends, leadership and ownership changes, new firm disclosures). AdvisorCheck was founded in 2019, is headquartered in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey with an office in Los Angeles, and raised a $1.8M seed round in June 2023. The company operates an application API at api.advisorcheck.com but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: arxo-io
providers.description: Arxo provides Law as Code infrastructure, writing statutes and regulations as executable models that run on case facts and return answers with the underlying provisions. The platform enables applications and AI agents to query versioned legal models, see where official text does not apply, and publish findings to a public register after notifying responsible offices.

providers.name: Certificial
providers.description: Certificial operates the Smart COI Network, a real-time certificate of insurance (COI) tracking, issuance and compliance platform used by requestors, insureds, and insurance agents and brokers. Instead of a static PDF certificate that goes stale the moment a policy changes, Certificial maintains a continuously monitored Smart COI that reflects policy-level changes as they happen and notifies every party to the relationship. The company sells two API products to software platforms — an Insurance Tracking API for pulling real-time, source-verified coverage data and COI documents into a host platform, and a COI Issuance API for InsurTech and agency-management vendors that need to generate and automatically reissue ACORD-form certificates. The platform API is live at my.certificial.com/api/ but is credential-gated, and no public API reference, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal is published — API access is arranged through a sales/reseller conversation.

providers.name: دادرس
providers.description: دادرس یک پلتفرم هوشمند حقوقی به زبان فارسی است که از هوش مصنوعی برای ارائه مشاوره حقوقی، جستجوی قوانین و آرای ایران، و مدیریت پرونده‌های حقوقی استفاده می‌کند. کاربران می‌توانند با پرسیدن سوالات حقوقی به فارسی، پاسخ‌های واضح همراه با ارجاع به متن قانون دریافت کنند. این سرویس شامل ابزارهای محاسبه‌گرهای حقوقی، تنظیم آنلاین دادخواست، لایحه و قرارداد، و امکان جستجوی پیشرفته در متون قانونی می‌باشد. هدف ارائه دستیار حقوقی هوشمند برای تسهیل دسترسی به اطلاعات حقوقی در ایران است.

providers.name: Bitsighttechnologies
providers.description: Bitsight is a cyber risk intelligence platform that provides real‑time monitoring of external attack surfaces, third‑party risk, and vulnerability data. Leveraging AI‑driven attribution and a massive data set of internet‑exposed assets, Bitsight helps enterprises assess and mitigate security risks across their supply chain, vendors, and internal assets. The platform offers continuous monitoring, risk scoring, and actionable insights for security, compliance, and risk management teams.

providers.name: Chronicled
providers.description: Chronicled is a San Francisco technology company that builds and administers the blockchain-powered MediLedger Network, a decentralized platform that automates business-rule enforcement and trusted data exchange between trading partners in the pharmaceutical and life sciences supply chain. Its solutions span DSCSA-compliant product verification, contracts and chargebacks, gross-to-net (GPO roster and rebate) reconciliation, and customer master data management for manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, health systems, and group purchasing organizations. Chronicled publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI; it operates a private B2B network and is backed by Pantera Capital.

providers.name: G-P
providers.description: G-P (Globalization Partners) is the recognized leader in global employment, providing a comprehensive platform to hire, manage, and pay employees and contractors in 180+ countries without setting up local entities. Their REST APIs enable companies to automate HR workflows, manage employment contracts, benefits, payroll, and compliance across international teams through EOR (Employer of Record) and Contractor products.

providers.name: OpenCorporates
providers.description: OpenCorporates is the world's largest open database of companies, providing a REST API for searching and retrieving company registration data, officer information, and corporate filings globally across more than 140 jurisdictions. The API enables access to company details, director and officer records, statutory filings, and corporate groupings, making it a primary resource for compliance, due diligence, investigative journalism, and corporate transparency.

providers.name: Signify
providers.description: Signify provides a comprehensive contract management platform that digitizes the entire workflow for sales, procurement, HR, finance, and front office operations. Users can create, manage, and store legally binding electronic contracts, automate approvals, and integrate with existing enterprise systems. The solution emphasizes security, compliance, and a seamless user experience across web and mobile, supporting digital signatures, document storage, and analytics to streamline business processes.

providers.name: VXT
providers.description: VXT provides AI-powered call and meeting note automation for law firms, turning conversations into structured legal paperwork, call recordings, time tracking, and email drafts. Integrated with major legal software, it aims to recover extra billable minutes and streamline workflow for lawyers.

providers.name: Flow
providers.description: Flow (Flow Engineering, operated by TRC Space Ltd) is a requirements-management platform built for hardware and systems engineering teams. It centers on a Systems Graph that connects requirements, design artifacts, tests, and components, with AI agents that continuously align CAD, simulation, code, and test — automating impact analysis, budget tracking, and compliance checking. Flow supports branching and merging of requirement baselines, iterative build gates, and an integration ecosystem spanning CAD (Onshape, Fusion 360, Siemens NX), simulation (Ansys), and dev tools (GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Slack, Notion, Confluence). It is SOC 2 Type II, NIST 800-171, and ITAR/EAR aligned with self-hosted and AWS GovCloud options. A first-party API exists (referenced in the changelog) but is gated behind login with no publicly published OpenAPI or developer documentation.

providers.name: Medallion
providers.description: Medallion is an AI-powered healthcare operations platform for provider credentialing, enrollment, and licensing, operated by FirstLayerAI, Inc. It positions itself as the AI operations partner powering healthcare's first real-time CVO (Credentialing Verification Organization), NCQA-certified, and serves provider groups, payers, health systems, RCM organizations, and digital health companies. Capabilities span provider data management, delegated credentialing, roster management, privileging, cross-state licensing, ongoing credential monitoring, and CredAlliance, its proprietary payer clearinghouse. Medallion is SOC 2 compliant and publishes a Trust Center. As of this profile there is no public developer API surface; enrichment captured the company's identity, compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: Trustdock
providers.description: TRUSTDOCK Inc. (株式会社TRUSTDOCK) is a Tokyo-based digital identity and eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) provider founded in November 2017. The company delivers high-precision, fast, and low-cost online identity verification and digital ID infrastructure via API, serving more than 300 enterprise and government clients across finance, insurance, ride-sharing and car-sharing, telecommunications (MNO/MVNO), real-estate crowdfunding, second-hand/reuse goods, recruitment, matching apps, and public-sector onboarding. TRUSTDOCK offers both browser-based and mobile-app-based verification flows, holds ISMS (ISO 27001) certification and the Japanese PrivacyMark, and participates in the OpenID Foundation Japan KYC Working Group and the FIDO Alliance. Its API documentation is provided to customers under NDA rather than published to a public developer portal.

providers.name: BankruptcyObserver
providers.description: Stay ahead of US business bankruptcies without repeatedly checking bankruptcy websites. Get next-morning alerts, verify changes against the court record, and connect your AI agent through MCP for case-specific answers. Standard and Heavy include a 7-day free trial. Cancel anytime.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Darrow
providers.description: Darrow is an AI legal-intelligence company (founded 2020, offices in New York, Miami, Arizona and Tel Aviv) that scans public real-world signals — regulatory filings, court dockets, incident reports, corporate disclosures and web behavior — to detect legal violations at scale, size the affected class, predict outcomes and value the resulting cases. Its platform serves plaintiff law firms (case origination, predictive litigation analytics, portfolio management, PlaintiffLink intake), insurers (predictive underwriting) and corporate compliance teams (Privacy Radar, listed in the Microsoft Marketplace). Darrow publishes no public developer program: the product is delivered through an Auth0-protected customer portal at portal.darrow.ai, and the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the OpenID Connect discovery document served by its identity tenant.

providers.name: Defense Unicorns
providers.description: Defense Unicorns is a defense-technology company that makes running modern software on military systems easy — from cloud to edge, satellites to submarines. Its UDS (Unicorn Delivery Service) platform is a secure-by-default, airgap-native software delivery stack built on Kubernetes and Zarf, bundling Istio, Keycloak, Authservice, Prometheus/Grafana, Vector/Loki, Falco and the Pepr policy engine. The company ships its developer surface as open-source CLIs and libraries — the UDS CLI, Pepr, Lula (compliance-as-code / OSCAL), and the Maru task runner — rather than a hosted REST API. Offerings span UDS Core, UDS Fleet, UDS Enterprise, software factories, compliance automation, and forward-deployed engineering. Backed by Sapphire Ventures.

providers.name: Firstbase
providers.description: Firstbase is an all-in-one startup operating system that helps founders form, run, and grow a US business from anywhere in the world. Its products cover incorporation (Firstbase Start for LLCs and C-Corps in Delaware, Wyoming, New York, Texas and more), ongoing compliance and registered-agent services (Firstbase Agent), bookkeeping, invoicing and tax-ready financials (Firstbase Accounting), tax filing, and a virtual business address (Firstbase Mailroom). Firstbase markets an embedded "Incorporation API" for platforms that want to offer company formation to their own users, but publishes no public developer documentation, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal for it. Firstbase is a venture-backed company (a16z portfolio) added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Mitigata
providers.description: Mitigata is an India-based, IRDAI-licensed integrated cyber resilience platform that bundles cyber insurance, 24x7 security operations, and compliance under one accountable pod. It offers smart cyber liability, D&O, E&O, crime and EPLI insurance; an in-house Bengaluru SOC with MDR, EDR/XDR, SIEM, SASE, ZTNA and DFIR; automated compliance for ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, DPDP, GDPR, HIPAA, RBI and SEBI-CSCRF; and Gordon AI, an autonomous AI SOC covering dark-web monitoring, attack-surface management, third-party risk and phishing simulation. Mitigata publishes eleven purpose-built APIs (cyber score, email security, asset discovery, phishing protect, dark-web scanner, security checklist, third-party risk, employee risk, attack assist, cyber insurance and claims) but gates technical onboarding behind a booked API walkthrough.

providers.name: AuditBoard
providers.description: AuditBoard (rebranded in 2026 as Optro) is an AI-powered GRC (governance, risk, and compliance) SaaS platform used by more than half of the Fortune 500 to run their audit, risk, and compliance programs. Its connected-risk suite spans Controls Management (SOX), OpsAudit (operational/internal audit), RiskOversight (enterprise/operational risk), CrossComply (IT risk and cybersecurity compliance), ESG, RegComply (regulatory compliance), and AI Governance. Optro exposes a developer platform at developer.auditboard.com (a login-gated ReadMe portal) for programmatic access, plus documented integrations with systems such as ServiceNow, Workiva, and Microsoft 365. AuditBoard was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched here from its public web surface; the API reference itself sits behind an end-user login, so no public OpenAPI is captured.

providers.name: IRALOGIX
providers.description: IRALOGIX is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania fintech that operates a cloud-native, white-label IRA (Individual Retirement Account) recordkeeping and administration platform for financial institutions — banks, wealth managers, brokerages, recordkeepers and advisors — who use it to offer digital IRA programs under their own brand. The platform covers onboarding, contributions, trading, distributions, rollovers, compliance monitoring and administration end to end, and the company markets "API-driven connectivity and real-time data flows" that integrate with existing custodial and recordkeeping infrastructure rather than replacing it. The developer surface is partner-gated: documentation at docs.iralogix.com sits behind Okta visitor authentication and the partner console at partner.iralogix.com behind an Auth0 tenant, so no public OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or SDK is published. The company states SSAE SOC 2 Type 1 and SSAE SOC 1 Type 2 attestation.

providers.name: Lizzyai
providers.description: Lizzy is a generative-AI platform for legal professionals, delivering a secure Gen AI workspace across all practice areas through both a web application and a Microsoft Word/Outlook add-in. It supports contract drafting, review, analysis, and proofreading, customizable legal workflows and playbooks, in-document citations, redlining and track-changes, and the handling of long, scanned, watermarked, and multiple documents. A multi-LLM approach routes each task to the most capable model, and firms can train a private model that embeds their own know-how. Built for enterprise IT with a zero-trust architecture, no training on customer data, PII anonymization, SSO via SAML and OAuth 2.0, and shared, VPC, or self-hosted deployment options.

providers.name: Risklytics
providers.description: Risklytics is an AI-native property and catastrophe risk company (Y Combinator Summer 2026, based in San Francisco, founded 2026 by Samuel Gold and Alexander Risio). It builds hyper-localized disaster risk models that simulate specific natural hazards - wildfire, flood, wind, earthquake, and debris runout - against individual home structures rather than ZIP-code averages, creating a per-structure digital twin from building footprints, lidar, and public records. Its Ember API returns property risk scores, modeled annual loss estimates, and retrofit-impact modeling used for insurance risk selection and portfolio triage (currently California-only, production model ember-1.3.0-firewall). The company also operates the FireCast platform and an AI-native brokerage for hard-to-place commercial insurance. API access is via a personal API key issued through the platform dashboard; there is no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or blog published to date, so this profile captures the company identity, the documented Ember API plans and authentication model, and the security posture of its web surface.

providers.name: Westlaw
providers.description: Westlaw, a Thomson Reuters legal research platform, provides AI‑enhanced tools, extensive case law, statutes, and practical guidance for law firms, businesses, and government agencies. Leveraging over 175 years of legal expertise, Westlaw delivers trusted research, drafting assistance, and compliance solutions across a wide range of practice areas.

providers.name: Aeroz
providers.description: Aeroz provides supply chain traceability and product authentication solutions for regulated goods. Their platform uses NFC/UHF chips and GS1 2D codes to give each unit a unique identity, recording custody events via GS1 EPCIS 2.0. It supports compliance with DSCSA, EU Digital Product Passport, battery regulations, and other global standards, offering a secure, end‑to‑end digital product passport and connected packaging.

providers.name: Docugami
providers.description: Docugami provides an AI-powered document automation platform that transforms unstructured business documents into actionable knowledge graphs. Their technology enables enterprises to extract, organize, and act on data locked in contracts, reports, and other files, supporting use cases such as contract lifecycle management, data extraction, and workflow automation. By leveraging proprietary AI, Docugami helps reduce manual effort, improve compliance, and accelerate decision‑making across industries.

providers.name: DroneClear Thailand
providers.description: DroneClear Thailand provides full-service drone registration and compliance in Thailand, handling CAAT and NBTC registration, pilot exam preparation, and liability insurance for visitors. Based in Hua Hin, they offer transparent pricing, detailed guides, and support to ensure safe drone operations under Thai regulations.

providers.name: Flinn
providers.description: Flinn (flinn.ai) is an AI-powered regulatory and quality platform for medical technology and in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) manufacturers. It automates post-market surveillance (PMS) and compliance obligations across global frameworks including the EU MDR, IVDR, and FDA 21 CFR requirements. The platform continuously monitors 15+ safety databases in a single click, performs AI-assisted literature evaluation, automates complaint handling, and generates audit-ready reports for low- to high-risk medical devices. Flinn is used by 200+ global MedTech and IVD organizations, is hosted exclusively on AWS in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) with data kept inside the EU, and is validated/certified against ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/TR 80002-2, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, the EU AI Act, and GDPR. Backed by HV Capital and Speedinvest. This profile has been enriched from Flinn's public web presence; the product is a closed SaaS application with no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Sovos
providers.description: Sovos provides a global, cloud‑based platform for tax compliance, regulatory reporting, and e‑invoicing. It helps enterprises automate indirect tax calculations, filing, and information reporting across more than 200 jurisdictions. The platform integrates with ERP, finance, and e‑commerce systems, offering APIs for real‑time tax determination, filing, and compliance analytics. Sovos serves Fortune‑500 companies and midsize businesses, delivering solutions for sales tax, VAT, GST, customs duties, and specialized reporting such as 1099, crypto tax, and unclaimed property.

providers.name: Vorlon
providers.description: Vorlon is an agentic ecosystem security platform that helps enterprises deploy AI agents and SaaS applications safely by protecting sensitive data in real time. The platform maps and monitors data flows between AI agents, enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, and cloud data stores, detecting threats, masking sensitive data in transit, and restricting agent access. Its patent-pending DataMatrix engine models the SaaS ecosystem — linking alerts, identities, APIs, data flows, and secrets — and a remote MCP server lets LLMs query security data and orchestrate investigations. Vorlon is backed by Accel and is SOC 2 Type II certified.

providers.name: AnwaltX
providers.description: AnwaltX is a KI‑gestützte Rechtsassistenz für Online‑Händler, Amazon‑Seller und Creator. Die Plattform analysiert hochgeladene Schreiben oder beschriebene Fälle, ermittelt Fristen, liefert rechtliche Einschätzungen und generiert Antwortentwürfe. Sie deckt Abmahnungen, Kontosperrungen, Vertragsprüfung, AGB‑Erstellung und DSGVO‑Compliance ab und bietet ein monatliches Abonnement von 64,99 €.

providers.name: Cozy Finance
providers.description: Cozy Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) risk-management protocol that helps onchain protocols unlock safety-seeking capital through composable, institutional-grade coverage. Its Cozy Safety Module (CSM) lets teams deploy onchain safety modules, rewards managers, and controllers that backstop capital against security incidents and market risk, using mechanisms such as tranching (junior/senior yield), reserves, and market-based protection contracts. The protocol is used by teams around protocols such as Euler, Lido, and Aave, and is backed by Polychain Capital, Electric Capital, Dragonfly, and Coinbase Ventures. The integration surface is Solidity smart contracts documented at csm-docs.cozy.finance, with TypeScript / ethers.js developer guides; there is no REST or HTTP API.

providers.name: Recast Software
providers.description: Extend the power of Configuration Manager, Intune, and more to achieve compliance and reclaim efficiency with Recast. Recast provides automation and compliance solutions for modern workplaces, integrating with Microsoft Endpoint Manager and other IT management tools.

providers.name: Tero
providers.description: Tero provides an agent‑native telemetry layer that connects read‑only to existing observability data stores. It continuously identifies costly waste, sensitive data exposure, and operational risks that traditional tools miss. By delivering actionable issue evidence, Tero helps organizations cut costs by 40‑60%, improve compliance, and enhance reliability across cloud and on‑prem environments. The platform offers a unified view of telemetry, automated issue detection, and integrated remediation actions, all without requiring changes to existing monitoring stacks.

providers.name: Anteroom
providers.description: Anteroom is a structured legal‑review tool that helps organizations assess AI launch compliance. It provides curated, up‑to‑date regulatory insights across jurisdictions, offering a searchable corpus of statutes, guidance, and case law. Users can input launch details to receive a tailored analysis of applicable regulations, obligations, and risk mitigations, supporting responsible AI deployment.

providers.name: Deloitte
providers.description: Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating through a network of member firms coordinated by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited (DTTL). The organization spans approximately 150 countries and territories, has more than 180 years of history (founded 1845), and serves roughly 90% of the Fortune Global 500. Deloitte organizes delivery across four primary service lines — Audit & Assurance, Consulting, Tax, and Legal — plus specialized cross-functional practices including Business Process Solutions and Global Employer Services. Consulting offerings cover Customer, Cyber, Engineering / AI & Data, Enterprise Technology & Performance, Finance Transformation, Human Capital, Strategy & Transactions, and Risk / Regulatory & Forensic. Deloitte Digital is the technology-and-experience practice with alliances spanning Salesforce, Adobe, SAP, Google Cloud, AWS, ServiceNow, Oracle, Shopify, Sitecore, and Genesys, and accelerators such as FrontOffice Advantage, Revenue Advantage, Agentic Marketing Cloud, CreativEdge, Blueprint, Content Studios, and TrustID. The organization serves six industries divided into twenty sectors: Consumer; Energy, Resources & Industrials; Financial Services; Government & Public Services; Life Sciences & Health Care; and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. Deloitte Insights is the organization's research-publishing surface, organized into eight research centers — Cross-Industry, Economics, Consumer, Energy & Industrials, Financial Services, Government & Public Services, Life Sciences & Health Care, and Tech, Media & Telecom — producing flagship series including Tech Trends, Global Human Capital Trends, Digital Media Trends, TMT Predictions, FSI Predictions, the Weekly Global Economic Outlook, and the annual Industry Outlooks. The Deloitte AI Institute drives applied-AI research and points of view. Deloitte does not publish a public developer API or open developer portal at the corporate level. The Deloitte US Consulting GitHub organization is small (5 visible repositories, mostly archived upstream forks; the original artifact is `beacon`, a first-party web-analytics packaging library in TypeScript). Reader-facing distribution flows through MyDeloitte (personalized content + newsletter subscriptions), Dbriefs (live webcasts with CPE credit), the Deloitte Insights Magazine, and the YouTube channel; no public RSS index page was discoverable on www.deloitte.com at the path published in legacy archives.

providers.name: une-education
providers.description: UNE (Unified Norms Engine) provides deterministic cross‑border computation and compliance infrastructure for autonomous agents. It offers multiple nodes covering customs tariffs, trade regulations, maritime fuel compliance, standards, legal dispute resolution, and sanctions screening, each accessible via Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints with OpenAPI 3.1 specifications. The platform delivers cryptographic proof of calculations, zero‑entropy query results, and supports public anonymous access as well as paid developer passes.

providers.name: Docket Alarm
providers.description: Docket Alarm provides a cloud‑based platform that aggregates and delivers federal, state, and intellectual‑property court filings. Attorneys and paralegals can search, receive alerts, and run analytics on litigation outcomes. The service offers a public Developer API for programmatic access to case data, pricing plans, and documentation, supporting legal research and workflow automation.

providers.name: Magier AI
providers.description: Magier AI provides end-to-end LLM cybersecurity solutions, offering compliance enforcement, risk management, and AI governance tools. Their platform includes AI pentesting, data redaction, policy generation, and audit-ready evidence across frameworks like ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, HIPAA, SOC 2, and GDPR. Targeting startups to enterprises, Magier AI helps organizations monitor AI vendor risk, enforce data controls, and streamline compliance reporting.

providers.name: Claim Done
providers.description: Claim Done provides Australians with easy-to-use, flat-fee legal document services, allowing users to generate letters of demand, tribunal applications, contract reviews and other consumer law documents online. The platform offers a simple questionnaire, instant drafts, and secure delivery, operating across all Australian states and territories. It is Australian owned and Sydney hosted, serving thousands of users with clear, affordable legal paperwork solutions.

providers.name: DecisionNext
providers.description: DecisionNext is a San Francisco-founded (2015) AI and machine-learning software company whose prescriptive analytics platform helps commodity-driven businesses decide what to buy and sell, when, at what price, and on what formula. The platform is organised in three layers — MarketView (transparent, commodity-specific price and supply forecasts built on USDA, CME and 100+ other market sources), Enterprise (scenario, formula, mix and timing optimisation through applications such as ScenarioLab, DecisionBuilder, MarketSim, DataMiner, YieldMax and MarketPosition) and Governance (executive accountability and market benchmarking). It serves food and agriculture (beef, pork, poultry, dairy, grains, edible oils) and natural resources (iron ore, thermal coal, LNG, copper, nickel, zinc, shipping). DecisionNext is delivered as a SaaS product — sold direct and through AWS Marketplace — and, as of this profiling pass, publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Diligent Pharma
providers.description: Diligent Pharma, Inc. is a Princeton, New Jersey clinical-trial quality and compliance company, founded in 2015, that operates a centralized vendor qualification and oversight platform for pharmaceutical and biotech sponsors and their service providers. Its Diligent360 platform unifies the vendor lifecycle — AI-assisted discovery across a network of 2,000+ clinical vendors, capability evaluation through standardized questionnaires, risk scoring across quality, compliance, cybersecurity and AI risk domains, qualification against ICH E6(R3) and GxP expectations, and ongoing oversight monitoring. Companion products DiligentRespond (automated vendor questionnaire response) and DiligentQualified (qualification package management) sit alongside a GxP audit services practice. The company raised an $8.27M Series A led by FCA Venture Partners in 2023 and has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list. The platform is delivered as an authenticated web application at 360.diligentpharma.com; Diligent Pharma publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: JSM Injury Firm
providers.description: Bitten or injured by a dog in California? Use this private checklist to understand what evidence to preserve, what insurance issues may matter, and whether attorney review may be appropriate. The site provides resources, a checklist, and contact information for legal consultation.

providers.name: Remofirst
providers.description: Remofirst is a global employment platform and Employer of Record (EOR) that helps companies hire, onboard, pay, and manage full-time employees and contractors across 185+ countries without establishing local legal entities. Its services span EOR employment, international contractor management, global multi-currency payroll, health insurance (RemoHealth), visa and work-permit support, background checks, and workforce administration. Remofirst is backed by QED Investors and positions itself as a lower-cost alternative in the global HR and payroll category. It publishes no public developer API today; integrations are delivered through partner connections (BambooHR, ADP Workforce Now, GoCardless).

providers.name: Sure
providers.description: Sure is an embedded insurance platform providing purpose-built REST APIs for distributing insurance products through digital channels. The platform enables brands, carriers, MGAs, and marketplaces to build, launch, and scale digital insurance programs covering quoting, binding, policy management, claims processing, payments, and compliance workflows across all 50 US states.

providers.name: Accordance Ai
providers.description: Accordance (operated by Agnetic Labs Inc.) is a San Francisco frontier AI platform built for tax, audit, and accounting professionals. Founded by researchers from the Stanford AI Lab, it provides a firmwide agentic AI platform that performs tax research with authoritative code, context, and citations, complex accounting analysis, and audit insight — with visible reasoning and verifiable source citations. Accordance is SOC 2 Type II certified, never trains on customer data, and is backed by Menlo Ventures, Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and New Enterprise Associates. The product surface is the Accordance application (app.accordance.ai); no public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: artificl-us
providers.description: Artificl is a one-person Michigan company building focused compliance trackers that your own AI assistant can operate. It offers a suite of specialized apps such as VendorPing, SubProof, LiftLog, HoodDue, DriverFile, DEAWatch, and CredCycle, each tracking expiring documents, permits, certifications, and regulatory compliance for various trades. The platform provides single-job expiry and document trackers, read‑only by default, with every action logged, enabling AI‑driven automation of compliance workflows.

providers.name: Chaoslabs
providers.description: Chaos Labs is a New York-based company building financial-intelligence and economic-security infrastructure for onchain markets. Its flagship product, Edge (Chaos Oracles), is a decentralized oracle protocol that unifies real-time price, risk, and proof-of-reserves data, delivering high-precision price feeds with an integrated risk engine plus automated, real-time risk-parameter optimization. Leading DeFi protocols including Aave, GMX, dYdX, Jupiter, Venus, Lido, Maker and Uniswap Foundation use Chaos Labs to help secure billions of dollars in value. Developer integration spans EVM, SVM, off-chain services and TradingView via docs.chaoslabs.xyz. Founded in 2021 by Omer Goldberg and Julian Lindinger, Chaos Labs is backed by Haun Ventures, Galaxy, PayPal Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, Lightspeed, Bessemer and others, and holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched from Chaos Labs' real public developer surface.

providers.name: Hummingbird
providers.description: Hummingbird is an AI-powered compliance operations platform for financial institutions and fintechs. It automates customer screening (sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media checks), transaction monitoring for financial crime, investigations and case management, and regulatory reporting including automated SAR, STR, and CTR filing. Hummingbird orchestrates risk and anti-money-laundering (AML) workflows across a connected app marketplace of 50+ integrations, and exposes custom two-way integration APIs provisioned through its partnerships team. The company is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified and backed by Homebrew.

providers.name: JSM Injury Firm
providers.description: JSM Injury Firm provides a free California Slip & Fall Evidence Checker, helping individuals understand what evidence to preserve after a slip and fall incident. The tool offers quick questions, legal guidance, and resources to assess potential claims, emphasizing privacy and on-screen results without email collection.

providers.name: Workhint
providers.description: Workhint is a work orchestration platform that uses AI to configure workflows, roles, and operations from modular components, helping teams manage flexible and on-demand workforces. The platform spans sourcing and onboarding, a workflow engine, tasks and projects, shifts and field visits, delivery management, auto-invoicing, global payments and payout workflows, contract management, and 1099 compliance. Backed by 500 Global and Softeq. API access and custom integrations are offered on the Enterprise plan, but no public developer portal or API documentation is published.

providers.name: DirectCase
providers.description: DirectCase provides AI‑powered legal research, offering verified citations across European case law and legislation. Users receive up to ten free queries without a credit card, and the platform supports lawyers, solicitors, barristers and trainees. The service aims to streamline legal workflows with accurate, sourced information.

providers.name: law-ai
providers.description: Law.AI is an AI-powered lawyer directory and matching platform that helps users find trusted, bar-verified attorneys across the United States. With over 838,000 verified lawyer profiles, the service lets users search by practice area, city, and state, and provides AI-driven matching to connect clients with the most suitable legal professionals. The platform is free to use and aims to expand access to justice.

providers.name: SecondSight
providers.description: SecondSight is a Bloomington, Indiana software company building a "vertical AI" operating system for cyber insurance and digital risk. Its Digital Risk Management Platform packages three SaaS surfaces — Company Workbench (digital asset inventory, privacy and vulnerability scanning, insurability preparation), Broker Workbench (client management, auto-complete applications, quote/bind automation, book value and portfolio analytics) and Underwriter Workbench (risk prediction, portfolio balancing, mitigation) — alongside Exposurescape, a digital-telematics engine for exposure detection and catastrophic-event forecasting. The company was founded in 2019, came out of stealth in 2022 with a seed round led by Tim Crown, and sells to brokers, carriers, MGUs and reinsurers. SecondSight publishes pricing, a SOC 2 security commitments page and a Better Stack status page for its Risk Workbench service, but as of this pass it operates no public developer program — no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind is published.

providers.name: Sourcemap
providers.description: Sourcemap is an enterprise supply chain transparency and due diligence software company, founded at the MIT Media Lab by Leonardo Bonanni and headquartered in New York. Its platform performs n-tier supply chain mapping, automated sub-supplier discovery, bill-of-materials mapping, transaction-level chain-of-custody traceability, supplier watchlist screening and AI document review, so that brands and manufacturers can meet regulatory obligations including the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA), the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD), CTPAT, conflict minerals rules and Section 232 tariff and customs enforcement. Sourcemap describes a real-time RESTful API and a data pipeline that moves structured data in both directions with SAP, Salesforce Net Zero Cloud, Databricks and the EU TRACES customs portal, but that API is sold and provisioned as part of an enterprise engagement: there is no public developer portal, no published API reference, no pricing page and no machine-readable contract on any Sourcemap host. Customers include Ferrero, Hershey, Woolworths and AG1.

providers.name: Strongkeep
providers.description: StrongKeep is a cybersecurity platform built for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) that lack a dedicated IT team or a large security budget. It bundles malware protection, scam and phishing protection, security-awareness ("secure habits") training, human-risk monitoring, and compliance readiness (such as Cyber Essentials) into a single dashboard, with most customers reportedly going live within 60 minutes. StrongKeep offers a free no-install security scan, plans starting at $39/month, and vertical solutions for healthcare clinics and professional-services firms. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. StrongKeep does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from its public web surface (identity, security.txt, and domain-security probes).

providers.name: Echo
providers.description: Echo is a software supply-chain security company that delivers vulnerability-free (CVE-free), secure-by-design base container images, language libraries, hardened virtual machines, serverless runtimes, and OS packages. Its artifacts are built as drop-in replacements so engineering teams eliminate known CVEs across their software supply chain without changing application code, cutting remediation toil and easing compliance with frameworks like FedRAMP, FIPS, PCI DSS, DORA, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Echo operates as a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) and publishes a Trust Center with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and FIPS 140-3 assurance. The company is backed by GGV Capital.

providers.name: Neo.Tax
providers.description: Neo.Tax is an AI-powered tax automation platform that helps enterprises and their accounting teams generate audit-ready R&D tax credit studies, software capitalization (ASC 350-40), and R&D capitalization (IRC Section 174) documentation. The platform ingests engineering and financial data from tools like Jira, GitHub, payroll systems, and Workday and uses large language models and agentic AI to qualify projects under IRC Section 41, eliminating the manual surveys and interviews that traditionally drive R&D tax credit work. Neo.Tax is backed by GV and Uncork Capital and delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS product; it operates a customer application, a help center, a public status page, and a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR) but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: DeepStream Technologies
providers.description: DeepStream Technologies (deep.stream) is a London-based AI-enhanced eSourcing and source-to-contract platform for mid-market procurement teams. It digitalizes buyer-to-supplier sourcing with best-of-breed eRFx, supplier discovery, supplier pre-qualification, eAuctions, contract management, management reporting, and AI-driven RFP generation and conversational analytics, aiming to help procurement teams work faster, reduce risk, and gain visibility while keeping implementation simple. Customers include Walkers Shortbread, BrewDog, Abbott, and Free Now. DeepStream does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation; integrations with ERP and PO systems are delivered as a service. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with public company and infrastructure signals.

providers.name: Linte
providers.description: Linte is a Brazilian legal-technology company offering an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform for large enterprises. Its product family spans Linte CLM for document automation and contract lifecycle governance, Linte AI for contract review that summarizes versions and flags risk against a customer playbook, Linte BI for contract analytics dashboards, and Linte Intake for legal demand intake and triage. The platform integrates natively with digital signature providers including ClickSign, DocuSign and D4Sign, and is sold to enterprise legal, procurement and compliance teams primarily in Brazil. Linte publishes no public API program, developer portal or API reference; its only public developer-facing artifacts are npm-published embeddable "Linte Docs" form components.

providers.name: Preamble
providers.description: Preamble provides cybersecurity and compliance solutions for generative AI, protecting against prompt injections, data leakage, and regulatory risks. Their platform offers policy enforcement, monitoring, and risk assessment tools tailored for AI developers and enterprises, ensuring safe and trustworthy AI deployments across various industries.

providers.name: BlockSec
providers.description: BlockSec is a Web3 security and compliance platform offering smart contract audits, infrastructure audits, blockchain penetration testing, AML/CFT compliance tools, and real‑time threat detection. Founded to protect decentralized applications and crypto enterprises, BlockSec provides a suite of products including Phalcon Security, Phalcon Compliance, MetaSleuth, and a public intelligence network for illicit fund monitoring.

providers.name: Docketwise
providers.description: Docketwise provides cloud-based immigration law practice management software, enabling attorneys to manage cases, clients, and documents efficiently. The platform offers tools for client intake, case tracking, document generation, and collaboration, helping firms streamline immigration workflows and improve client experiences.

providers.name: Elpha Secure
providers.description: Elpha Secure is a New York-based cyber insurance managing general agent (MGA) for small and midsize businesses that bundles a first-party cybersecurity software agent with the insurance policy itself. The Elpha Agent ships endpoint detection and response, Malware Guard anti-malware, encrypted offsite backup, multi-factor authentication for remote desktop access, email security (ES Mail), financial fraud detection, vulnerability and security-posture scoring, and XDR integrations with SentinelOne, Sophos, Trend Micro and CrowdStrike, all managed from the Elpha Secure Portal. Policies are distributed through appointed brokers who quote and bind in the broker portal. Elpha Secure publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; its Terms of Service define "Elpha Secure API's" as SOAP- or REST-based interfaces made available to customers and integrators under agreement.

providers.name: DMCA.com
providers.description: DMCA.com is a content protection and takedown service founded in 2006. It helps creators, brands, and individuals worldwide remove stolen content from the internet. The company offers free reviews and a range of protection plans, leveraging a team of experts to enforce copyrights and combat piracy.

providers.name: Enzai
providers.description: Enzai is an enterprise AI governance platform that helps organizations adopt AI while managing regulatory and operational risk. Its product suite spans agentic AI governance (real-time analysis, risk flagging, and agent-sprawl management), AI use-case intake and approval workflows, a centralized AI registry inventorying first- and third-party AI systems, and compliance frameworks that map AI initiatives to the EU AI Act, GDPR, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001. Enzai is headquartered in Belfast with a London office, is ISO 27001 certified, and is backed by venture capital including Seedcamp. No public API or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Zinc
providers.description: Zinc is a UK-founded, Y Combinator and Seedcamp-backed background checking platform that automates pre-employment screening for HR and talent teams. It runs criminal record checks across 195 countries, employment and reference verification, financial and adverse-media screening, right-to-work and qualification checks, delivering results in hours rather than weeks with an average three-day turnaround. Zinc integrates with major ATS and HRIS platforms (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, HiBob, SAP SuccessFactors and others) and is ISO 27001, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials, GDPR and FCRA aligned. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched from Zinc's public web surface; no public developer API or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Streamline
providers.description: Streamline AI provides a legal front‑door and intake automation platform for in‑house legal teams. It streamlines request management, workflow automation, matter management, analytics, dynamic document generation, and AI‑powered features like email intake, knowledge bot, and contract intelligence, helping legal operations scale efficiently.

providers.name: Vesence
providers.description: Vesence builds agentic AI for professional-services firms that works directly inside Microsoft Office. Its agents operate in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, plus a web app, reviewing emails, documents and projects before they leave the firm and turning Microsoft Word into a purpose-built workspace for high-stakes drafting, quality assurance and knowledge work. Vesence connects to SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Teams and document-management systems so agents work with a firm's existing files and context, with every edit traceable through tracked changes. Trusted by law firms, banks and investors, Vesence targets transactional legal work such as fund formation, M&A and corporate matters. It is a Y Combinator-backed startup surfaced through the venture portfolios of Creandum and Emergence Capital.

providers.name: Aatmunn
providers.description: Aatmunn (formerly Guardhat, founded 2014 in Detroit and headquartered in Livonia, Michigan) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform for frontline and deskless workers. Its SPANR / Industrial Internet of People (IIoP) platform unifies workers, workplaces, and assets into one real-time system, connecting devices from any manufacturer and layering AI-driven insights for predictive hazard detection, emergency response, inspections, and compliance. Products include Inspections, Lone Worker Safety, Human Condition Monitoring, Gas Detection, Control Access Zoning, and Asset Tracking, serving 250+ companies across high-risk industries such as oil & gas, chemicals, mining & infrastructure, manufacturing, utilities, and warehousing & logistics. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and is maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; Aatmunn publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: filehub GmbH
providers.description: filehub GmbH provides a no‑code automation platform that connects apps, portals and software to automate document flows such as invoice download, data extraction, archiving and workflow management. It serves finance, procurement, sales and operations teams with templates, integrations and compliance‑ready processes, offering a free plan and paid tiers for enterprises.

providers.name: Rates and Limits
providers.description: A free, keyless open-data publisher exposing US federal and state tax, payroll, benefits, and wage figures as JSON. Every figure ships bundled with provenance: the exact quoted sentence from the governing government document, byte offsets, sha256-stamped source snapshots, and last-verified dates.

providers.name: AdmitBase
providers.description: AdmitBase is a professional-school admissions data platform. It compares an applicant's GPA and standardised test score against the admitted‑student figures each school itself published, and returns a 0‑100 match score classified as Safety, Target, Reach or Far Reach. See your real chances at every law, medical, and dental school — your GPA and test score against admitted‑student data from official disclosures.

providers.name: BetterView Marketplace
providers.description: Betterview is a market-leading Property Intelligence platform that delivers actionable insights to property & casualty insurance underwriters, agents, and insureds to increase efficiency and profitability. Its API lets carriers order and retrieve property profiles enriched with the Roof Spotlight Index (RSI), peril risks, flags, and third-party Partner Connect data, subscribe properties to PropertyPulse monitoring, and query PropertyNow pre-processed datasets by address or coordinates. Betterview integrates with core insurance systems including Guidewire (a Marketplace accelerator for PolicyCenter 10), Duck Creek, and Socotra, and supports SSO, Secure FTP, ImageRight drop, an embeddable geospatial iframe UI, and an External Data Warehouse (EDW) SQL connection.

providers.name: Deeploi
providers.description: Deeploi (deeploi GmbH) is a Berlin-based all-in-one IT management (ITSM) platform for mid-sized businesses and startups, primarily across the DACH region. It centralizes employee onboarding and offboarding, device and inventory management, software and license/account administration, cybersecurity and compliance policies, and unlimited expert IT support in a single dashboard priced per active employee. Deeploi operates an Information Security Management System aligned with ISO/IEC 27001 and is GDPR compliant, publishing its posture through a Kertos-powered Trust Center. The company is backed by Atomico. Deeploi does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: DocuWare
providers.description: DocuWare provides cloud‑based document management and workflow automation solutions for businesses of all sizes. Its platform enables secure capture, storage, indexing, and retrieval of documents, along with advanced features like intelligent document processing, electronic signatures, and integration with popular enterprise applications. DocuWare helps organizations streamline processes, improve compliance, and enhance productivity through a scalable, SaaS‑delivered service.

providers.name: HData
providers.description: HData is the AI-native operating system for energy regulation. Founded in 2018 by Hudson Hollister, the platform turns disconnected federal and state regulatory filings, dockets, and proceedings from sources such as FERC, EIA, and state utility commissions into standardized, citable, machine-readable data. It combines centralized regulatory data, domain-specific AI trained on more than 20 million citable documents, and purpose-built tools — including HData Analytics, Regulatory Intelligence, Gateway for FERC data extraction, and Data Request Management — to help utilities, regulators, advocates, advisory firms, financial institutions, and large energy customers accelerate rate cases, resource planning, compliance reporting, and policy research.

providers.name: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance)
providers.description: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance) is a Chicago-based commercial trucking insurance company delivering modern, data-driven coverage for small and mid-size fleet operators. Its flagship HDVI Shift product uses integrated telematics and safety data to dynamically price premiums, rewarding safe driving with monthly discounts of up to 20 percent, and its Fleet Portal gives fleets tools to improve safety, reduce risk, maintain compliance, and lower costs. HDVI was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it operates a customer-facing Fleet Portal and telematics/ELD/dash-cam partner integrations rather than an open developer program. This profile captures the company's real public identity, its published llms.txt, its SOC 2 Type 2 compliance posture, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: IVIX
providers.description: IVIX is an AI-powered financial-intelligence platform that analyzes publicly available data at scale to surface hidden and unreported business activity, helping government tax authorities and law-enforcement agencies combat the shadow economy, tax evasion, and financial crime. The platform ingests open and third-party data to detect non-compliant businesses, quantify unreported revenue (including short-term rentals and crypto markets), and map illicit networks for enforcement teams. IVIX is a closed, government-facing product — it is sold and deployed with authorities rather than exposed as a public self-serve API — and it is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified for information security. Backed by Insight Partners; headquartered in New York with former IRS Commissioner Charles Rettig on its board of advisors.

providers.name: SwiftComply
providers.description: SwiftComply is a cloud compliance-management platform for water utilities and municipalities, used by more than 700 organizations across North America to run their Backflow prevention, Stormwater (MS4), Industrial Pretreatment, and FOG (Fats, Oils, and Grease) programs. The software replaces paper and spreadsheet workflows with online program management, direct customer and service-provider reporting, real-time compliance dashboards, audit-ready timestamped record keeping, and pre-configured state reporting. SwiftComply advertises API integrations with GIS, utility billing, and other municipal platforms, and has held SOC 2 Type II certification since October 2021. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API description was found during enrichment.

providers.name: TimeSolv
providers.description: TimeSolv provides cloud‑based time tracking, billing, and practice management software for law firms and professional services. Its platform automates billable hour capture, invoicing, trust accounting, client portal, and integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, NetDocuments, Dropbox, LawPay and AI tools. TimeSolv aims to improve efficiency, compliance, and revenue visibility for legal practices.

providers.name: Bloomfilter
providers.description: Bloomfilter is a process intelligence platform that gives enterprises end-to-end visibility, traceability, and control over how AI agents and humans execute software delivery work. It unifies data across development and design tools such as Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, and Figma into a structured, AI-enabled data stream and builds a connected process graph across the software development lifecycle. Teams use Bloomfilter to govern hybrid human-agent workflows through process mining, compliance monitoring, cycle-time analysis, and performance measurement, so leaders can see how work actually flows and where value is created or lost. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: DSGVO.pro
providers.description: DSGVO.pro offers a free compliance scanner for German websites, checking up to 33 GDPR‑related modules such as DSGVO, TDDDG, KI‑VO, BFSG and BGB.
