The tool runs in about 60 seconds without registration, generating cookie‑banners and compliance reports. It aims to help site owners avoid fines by providing automated privacy audits and detailed legal references.

providers.name: Lexion
providers.description: Lexion is an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform that centralizes agreements in an intelligent repository, extracts key terms and dates, and drives no-code intake and approval workflows across legal, sales, procurement, finance, and HR. Founded in 2019 out of the Allen Institute for AI, Lexion was acquired by Docusign in May 2024 for ~$165M and folded into Docusign's Intelligent Agreement Management (IAM) platform and Docusign Navigator. Lexion exposes an enterprise, sales-led integration API but does not publish a self-serve, openly documented public API.

providers.name: Microbilt
providers.description: Microbilt is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: g2-catalog) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: ankar.ai
providers.description: Ankar is an AI operating system built for patent professionals, covering the full patent lifecycle: idea generation and patentability assessment, drafting of invention disclosures and applications, prosecution including office-action responses and strategy, and protection through infringement monitoring and competitive intelligence. It also provides small-molecule and sequence analysis, claim charts, research intelligence, and traceable citations to guidelines and case law. Customers are patent law firms and in-house IP teams (AmLaw 100 firms and Fortune 500 corporations), with 1,000+ users. Ankar is SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001:2022 certified and does not train AI models on customer data. It is enterprise-sold (book-a-demo) and publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Closinglock
providers.description: Closinglock is an Austin, Texas fintech and fraud-prevention company whose platform secures the money movement and identity checks inside a residential real estate closing. Title companies, real estate attorneys, agents, underwriters and their buyers and sellers use it to share wire instructions over an authenticated channel instead of email, verify identity and bank-account ownership before funds move, collect and disburse funds through SecurePay digital payments, retrieve and verify mortgage payoff statements, manage and e-sign closing documents, run two-way text messaging with the parties to a file, and evidence FinCEN and ALTA Best Practices obligations. The company announced SOC 2 Type II certification in August 2023 and raised a $34M Series B led by Sageview Capital in January 2025. Closinglock ships integrations into the major title production systems — SoftPro, RamQuest and ResWare — plus a DocuSign e-signature partnership, but those integrations are built bilaterally with each vendor: as of this profile Closinglock publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: DigitalOwl
providers.description: DigitalOwl is an AI-powered platform that transforms unstructured medical records into structured, actionable data for the life insurance, property & casualty insurance, and legal industries. Its products (View, Triage, Connect, Chat, Workflows, and Case Notes) automate medical record review, summarization, triage, and data extraction to accelerate underwriting, claims processing, and legal demand-package analysis. The Connect Data API maps source documents, classifications, and medical mentions (conditions, procedures, medications) into structured layers for integration into existing carrier and law-firm systems. DigitalOwl operates on AWS and Google Cloud with SOC 2 (Type II), HIPAA, and GDPR compliance. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Geordie AI
providers.description: Geordie AI is an enterprise AI governance platform that gives organizations visibility into and control over the autonomous AI agents deployed across their environments. It discovers agents across code, cloud, endpoints, and SaaS; maps each agent's posture (permissions, tools, MCP connections, and system prompts); provides behavioral observability with continuous audit trails and anomaly detection; delivers risk intelligence mapped to standards such as OWASP, NIST, ISO 42001, and the EU AI Act; and offers Beam, a real-time remediation layer that applies deterministic controls at the agent level. Geordie raised a $30M Series A and is used by enterprises including Xapo Bank, Fitch Group, Synthesia, AlphaSense, Owkin, OakNorth, and A+E Global Media. The company is SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and General Catalyst and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Geordie publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Bloomberg Financial Solutions
providers.description: Bloomberg Financial Solutions encompasses the full suite of Bloomberg financial data, analytics, and technology products designed to support front, middle, and back office workflows across asset management, banking, insurance, and corporate treasury. Solutions include market data, risk analytics, portfolio management, trading, compliance, and regulatory reporting capabilities.

providers.name: Relyance Ai
providers.description: Relyance AI is an AI-native data security, AI security, and privacy platform that maps data flows from source code through cloud and SaaS systems to AI models. Its core product, Lyo, acts as a "data defense engineer" providing real-time visibility into where sensitive data lives and moves, who accesses it, and how to remediate risk. The platform unifies data security (sensitive-data discovery, classification, and exfiltration detection), AI security (AI agent inventory, MCP server discovery, agentic AI risk), and privacy automation (DSRs, ROPAs, DPIAs, and consent management). Relyance AI is backed by Menlo Ventures.

providers.name: Verbal
providers.description: Verbal (tryverbal.com), from Salusive Health, is an AI-powered clinical compliance and quality-assurance platform for healthcare organizations. It automatically audits patient interactions — phone and video calls, telehealth visits, AI-agent conversations, and clinical chart notes — against customizable regulatory and quality checklists, scoring compliance in real time and surfacing gaps for supervisors and QA teams. Verbal connects to communications and EHR platforms including RingCentral, NICE, Zoom, Five9, Healthie, Epic, and Athena, and ships a Chrome extension for clinicians. It publishes a healthcare compliance posture — HIPAA compliant, HITRUST certified, CPRA, BAAs with all customers, PII redaction and US data residency. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API — the API language on its site describes Verbal consuming partner platform APIs, not an API it publishes, and there is no developer portal, reference, machine-readable spec, or SDK on any Verbal host. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Ivo
providers.description: Ivo (Ivo AI, Inc., formerly Latch) is an AI-powered contract intelligence platform built for in-house legal teams at enterprises. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in San Francisco, Ivo delivers three integrated products that share one AI engine: Ivo Review (a Microsoft Word add-in that applies a company's playbooks clause-by-clause to produce surgical redlines), Ivo Assistant (an agentic AI for drafting, cross-contract Q&A, and legal research) and Ivo Intelligence (an AI-native repository, powered by its AiRE engine, that turns existing contract libraries into queryable business intelligence). Customers include Uber, Shopify, IBM, Atlassian, Canva, Reddit and Pinterest. Ivo is enterprise-only with custom pricing and no public developer API; it publishes a canonical llms.txt, a Trust Center (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, GDPR, CCPA), and a responsible-disclosure security.txt.

providers.name: NexMind
providers.description: NexMind (operating as NexLaw) is a legal AI platform for U.S. litigators and law firms, offering secure, hallucination-free AI that drafts, summarizes, and researches legal work up to 10x faster. Its products include NeXa (AI legal research and drafting assistant), ChronoVault (evidence centralization and automated case timelines), TrialPrep (trial preparation workspace for arguments and witness outlines), and a real-time Courtroom Assistant, with capabilities spanning citation-backed legal deep research, deposition and document analysis, case chronology building, legal memo drafting, and contract and breach analysis. NexLaw is a direct-to-user SaaS product; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Structura
providers.description: Structura is a web-based visual domain modeling and code generation tool built by Metadev (metadev.pro). Architecture teams and software factories design class/domain models graphically or textually, refine them with the Zeus voice/text AI assistant, validate them for compliance and architectural consistency, and export deterministic, production-ready code for stacks such as Angular, .NET and Java, including custom generators that codify a team's conventions and policies. Its documentation also describes an MCP server for connecting AI tools to models.

providers.name: Case Status
providers.description: Case Status is a Charleston, South Carolina legal technology company, founded in 2018 by Andy Seavers and Lauren Gulley, that builds an AI-powered client engagement, experience, and communication platform for modern law firms. It delivers a branded, mobile-first client portal (iOS and Android), a CMS-integrated secure messaging hub with 1:1, bulk, and automated options, AI-driven Client Intelligence (message urgency triage, response recommendations, case summarization, sentiment prediction, and translation across 140+ languages), and client satisfaction analytics such as NPS, Predictive NPS, and CSAT. Case Status integrates with leading case management systems including Clio, Litify, MyCase, Neos, Filevine, SmartAdvocate, Docketwise, PracticePanther, SmokeBall, CASEpeer, MerusCase, CoCounselor, Salesforce, NuLaw, Matterly, and Zapier, plus a Chrome extension for attorneys. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars.

providers.name: Dropsuite
providers.description: Dropsuite, now a NinjaOne company, is a cloud backup, archiving, and recovery platform built for managed service providers (MSPs) and their small-to-midsize business customers. It provides automated backup and one-click restore for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, email, and website/database data, plus long-term email archiving with legal hold, eDiscovery, and journaling for compliance. Partners manage tenants through a multi-tenant portal and can automate provisioning, reporting, and reconciliation through a partner REST API gated to Direct Partners and Distributors (credentials issued in the Partner Portal under Settings -> API Settings). Dropsuite was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kroll Bond Rating Agency
providers.description: Kroll Bond Rating Agency (KBRA) is a full-service credit rating agency founded in 2010 by Jules Kroll and headquartered in New York, with offices in Dresher PA, Frederick MD, Chicago, Dublin, London, and Tokyo. KBRA is registered with the U.S. SEC as a Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization and with ESMA and the UK FCA through its Irish and UK entities. It has issued 96,000+ ratings covering $4.78 trillion of rated issuance across ABS, CMBS, RMBS, structured credit, corporates, financial institutions, funds, insurance, project finance, public finance, and sovereigns. KBRA distributes ratings and analytics commercially through the KBRA Analytics product family — Ratings Feed, Credit Intelligence, Direct Lending Deals, Premium, Credit Profile (KCP), and Financial Intelligence (KFI). KBRA publishes no public API or developer portal; machine access is contract-gated and delivered as bulk feeds over email/FTP/SFTP, through the Snowflake Marketplace, or via Bloomberg, Aladdin, and FactSet.

providers.name: Marlo Technologies
providers.description: Marlo is a maritime ERP platform for dry bulk, tanker, and commercial shipping companies, unifying chartering, voyage management, finance, banking, and compliance in a single system. Operators use Marlo to plan charters, track voyage operations and cargo, model voyage P&L and cashflow, run valuations and credit scoring, manage loans and covenants, hold multi-currency accounts with FX transfers and corporate cards, and handle sanctions screening, emissions tracking, and CII rating management. Marlo is a Techstars-backed company and holds SOC 2 (AICPA) certification. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass the company exposes a customer web application (app.marlo.co) but publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Actualyze AI
providers.description: Actualyze AI is an enterprise AI governance and management company building tools that give organizations the visibility and control they need to adopt AI at scale without slowing their teams down. Founded by Rafi Khardalian (CEO) and Sean Lynch (CTO) — veterans of building and operating distributed systems at global scale — the company designs for regulated industries from day one, embedding compliance, defense-in-depth data protection, comprehensive audit logging, and continuous monitoring into the platform rather than bolting it on. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Built
providers.description: Built (Built Technologies) is an AI-powered real estate and construction finance platform that connects capital and information across the construction lending ecosystem. It serves banks, credit unions, private credit firms, owners, developers, and general contractors with construction loan administration, deal origination and underwriting, project financials, invoice and lien-waiver management, compliance tracking, and payments. Founded over a decade ago and headquartered in Nashville and New York, Built operates on one of the largest connected datasets in real estate finance and integrates with Procore, Sage Intacct, Yardi, QuickBooks, Encompass, nCino, and DocuSign. It is backed by Fifth Wall and Index Ventures. This profile was enriched from Built's public developer and trust surfaces; Built publishes an integrations directory, identity/SSO, a status page, and a trust center, but does not expose a public REST API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: CARET Legal
providers.description: CARET Legal provides cloud‑based legal practice management software designed to streamline case handling, automate workflows, and integrate billing, document management, and client communication. The platform serves law firms of all sizes, offering features such as case management, reporting and analytics, secure document storage, and mobile access, all hosted securely in the cloud.

providers.name: Feroot
providers.description: Feroot Security is a Toronto-based cybersecurity company providing AI-powered client-side (browser) security and compliance automation for websites and mobile apps. Its platform gives organizations visibility into the third-party JavaScript, trackers, cookies, and data flows running in the browser, and automates compliance with PCI DSS 4.0.1 (requirements 6.4.3 script inventory and 11.6.1 tamper detection), HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and 50+ global regulations. Products include DXComply (privacy compliance and consent auditing), PaymentGuard (PCI DSS 4.0.1 automation for payment pages), and DXSecure (real-time client-side script security against formjacking, Magecart, and data exfiltration). Feroot is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and a PCI Security Standards Council Associate Member. Backed by Y Combinator, True Ventures, Haystack, and Stonemill Ventures.

providers.name: Leah
providers.description: Leah, formerly ContractPodAi and legally ContractPod Technologies Limited, is a London-headquartered enterprise agentic AI company that unifies contract lifecycle management, legal transformation, procurement, and finance operations into a single autonomous system. Its Leah Agentic OS platform provides skills-based orchestration, agentic workflows, a natural-language app builder, a library of domain-specific legal, contracting, procurement, and finance agents, and the Leah Maestro enterprise orchestrator. Leah is a five-time Gartner CLM Visionary, is SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, and is used by enterprises including PwC, KPMG, Philips, Alaska Airlines, MUFG, and Cushman & Wakefield. Leah ships pre-built connectors and describes open REST APIs for enterprise integration, but maintains no public developer portal or published API reference — API access is unlocked through the enterprise contract.

providers.name: LegalOS
providers.description: LegalOS is an AI-native U.S. immigration law practice based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Founded by Matthew Asir (CEO), Rachel Asir (COO) and Claire Jutabha (CTO), the company pairs proprietary legal software with licensed immigration attorneys to prepare employment-based visa and green-card petitions — H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, O-1 and TN visas, plus EB-1A, EB-1C and EB-2 NIW green cards. AI agents draft petition narratives, assemble supporting evidence and anticipate USCIS objections, with every filing reviewed by a licensed attorney before submission. LegalOS is delivered as a service through a customer web application at app.legalos.ai; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Exactera
providers.description: Exactera is a corporate tax technology and advisory company that pairs AI-powered software with expert tax professionals to help multinational corporations manage the full corporate tax lifecycle. Its SaaS platform and services span transfer pricing compliance and benchmarking, R&D tax credits, fixed-asset depreciation, indirect (sales and use) tax advisory, tax provision, and the RoyaltyStat royalty-rate and transfer-pricing data platform. Exactera automates documentation, benchmarking studies, and regulatory reporting so tax and finance teams can reduce audit exposure and meet global compliance requirements. Backed by Insight Partners, the company serves enterprise tax departments and advisory firms worldwide.

providers.name: Mabel
providers.description: Mabel is a healthcare technology company (Irvine, California; backed by 500 Global) that helps Medicare accountable care organizations (ACOs) enroll and engage beneficiaries. Its platform is a market leader in voluntary alignment, used by roughly one in three ACOs, and spans four core solutions: Voluntary Alignment (campaign execution, response processing, analytics, and compliance auditing for LEAD, ACO REACH, and GUIDE programs), Health Surveys (social determinants of health screenings, NPS, and custom surveys with CMS-formatted reporting), Beneficiary Notifications (compliance notices via email, mail, or SMS with audit-ready tracking), and Letters From Your Doctor (provider-based outreach for enrollment, surveys, and appointments). Mabel is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. No public developer API or SDK surface is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, compliance posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Neostella
providers.description: Neostella provides enterprise legal case management software, offering a comprehensive platform that includes case management, document management, analytics, reporting, time tracking, document generation, intake CRM, AI solutions, workflow automation, and integrations. Designed for law firms and in‑house legal teams, the SaaS solution helps streamline legal processes, improve efficiency, and support practice areas such as personal injury, mass tort, veterans affairs, social security, immigration, and family law.

providers.name: Urbint
providers.description: Urbint builds AI-powered operational resilience software for gas, electric and telecom utilities, predicting and preventing incidents before they happen across three product lines: Worker Safety, Damage Prevention (including a modern 811 locate-ticket management system), and Emergency Preparedness & Response / storm response. Its "Model of the World" fuses weather, topography, environmental, community and infrastructure data with a customer's own work, asset and outage data to score the risk on individual jobs and locate tickets. Urbint raised venture funding from Energy Impact Partners, Piva Capital, Energize Ventures, Blue Bear Capital, National Grid Partners, Fifth Wall, Salesforce Ventures and S2G, acquired Opvantek, WRM Software, Competers and iRestore, and was itself acquired by Itron for $325M in a deal announced 6 October 2025. Urbint ships no public API program; its only public developer surface is a first-party npm design system, @urbint/cl, which bundles a local-stdio MCP server.

providers.name: Xtype
providers.description: xtype is an automated governance platform for ServiceNow, giving enterprises visibility, control, orchestration, and compliance across every instance in their ServiceNow estate — tracking changes, access decisions, and configurations and enforcing policy in real time. Products include xtype Enterprise and the free xtype View. The company is backed by ServiceNow Ventures, Columbia Capital, Norwest Venture Partners, Inner Loop Capital, and SaaS Venture Capital, with offices in Covina (CA), Tel Aviv, and Vienna. xtype publishes no public developer API: api.xtype.io is a live Kong gateway with no publicly documented routes.

providers.name: 1touch.io
providers.description: 1touch.io is an enterprise data-security and data-intelligence vendor whose Kontxtual platform (previously shipped as Inventa) performs automated, near real-time discovery, classification, mapping and cataloging of sensitive data across cloud, on-premises, SaaS and IBM z/OS mainframe environments. The platform combines passive network analysis, ML/NLP classification and an LLM-driven contextual graph to deliver enterprise DSPM, attribute-based access control, access intelligence, DLP for streaming data, mainframe security posture management, cryptographic discovery and AI security. The technology is also OEM-distributed by IBM as Guardium Discover and Classify. Everpure (formerly Pure Storage, NYSE: PSTG) completed its acquisition of 1touch.io on 2026-05-11. Product documentation is published to a MadCap Central portal that requires a customer login, and no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is available.

providers.name: Henchman
providers.description: Henchman is a legal knowledge and contract-drafting AI platform that surfaces a firm's own past clauses and definitions from its document management system directly inside Microsoft Word, Outlook, and Copilot. It connects to legal DMS platforms (iManage, NetDocuments, SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive, OpenText eDocs), extracts and ranks clauses and definitions, and adds a secure multi-LLM AI clause assistant on top. Henchman was acquired by LexisNexis in 2024 and is being integrated into Lexis+ AI and Lexis Create+. Henchman is delivered primarily as add-ins and DMS connectors; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Pointone
providers.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

providers.name: HelloVerify
providers.description: HelloVerify is India's leading background verification (BGV) and employee screening company, delivering fast, accurate, and compliant primary-source verification for employment, education, healthcare credentialing, immigration, and enterprise workforce programs. The platform has completed 20M+ verifications for 2000+ organizations across 120+ countries, offering AI-powered background checks, customer KYC with identity and liveness, vendor due diligence (Certifier), and instant messaging-based verification (HelloV). HelloVerify operates an audited information-security and compliance program (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, Cyber Essentials, GDPR) and serves regulators, enterprises, SMBs, and applicants worldwide. Added to the API Evangelist network as a dcvc portfolio company; no public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Issa
providers.description: Issa Compass is a software platform that simplifies Thailand visa applications, operated by Issara Platforms Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) and Issa Systems Co, Ltd. (Bangkok). The platform helps users identify which Thai visa they qualify for and manages the end-to-end application process: a two-minute eligibility questionnaire, document verification and pre-qualification checks, real-time tracking of requirements against thousands of criteria, and a money-back guarantee if a pre-qualified application is rejected. Supported visa types include the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), Long-Term Resident (LTR), Retirement, Spouse, and Student visas. Issa is a portfolio company of 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Quatrix (Maytech)
providers.description: Quatrix, operating under the Maytech brand, provides secure file transfer, automated data acquisition, and compliant data sharing solutions for enterprises across industries such as finance, healthcare, and media. Their platform offers SFTP hosting, secure file sharing, large‑file transfers, and data rooms, emphasizing PCI compliance and robust security features.

providers.name: Afilio
providers.description: Afilio (Afilio - Gesellschaft für Vorsorge mbH) is a Berlin-based digital provision platform ("Vorsorgeplattform") that helps German families prepare for emergencies, care situations, and death. Through a paid membership, users create legally valid advance directives (Patientenverfügung), healthcare powers of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht), and wills (Testament), and maintain a digital inventory of documents and assets. A central emergency card gives doctors and relatives 24/7 access to critical medical and provision information, and Afilio also assists with care-level (Pflegegrad) applications and expert consultation. Over four million families use the GDPR-compliant service. Afilio is a consumer (B2C) platform and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public product, legal, and security surface. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Anduin
providers.description: Anduin (Anduin Transactions) is a private-markets technology company that digitizes investor onboarding and fund operations for venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds. Its platform replaces paper-based subscription workflows with electronic fund subscription documents, secure data rooms, investor data management, an engagement hub, an integration hub, automated data extraction, and e-signature. The company reports 1,305+ funds served, $244B+ capital raised, and 74,000+ investors subscribed. Anduin publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile captures its public company, trust, and security surfaces (Trust Center, RFC 9116 security.txt, and domain-security posture). Backed by 8vc; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Bloomberg Instant Messaging
providers.description: Bloomberg Instant Messaging (IB) is a secure, compliant messaging platform embedded in the Bloomberg Terminal and accessible via Bloomberg Anywhere. It enables real-time communication between financial professionals globally, with message archiving, compliance monitoring, and integration capabilities. Bloomberg also provides B-Chat for broader enterprise messaging connectivity.

providers.name: Bloomberg Message
providers.description: Bloomberg Message is the core messaging service within the Bloomberg Terminal ecosystem, enabling financial professionals to communicate securely through the Bloomberg IB (Instant Bloomberg) messaging system. It provides a compliant, archived communication channel for trading desks, asset managers, and financial institutions to exchange information, research, and trade-related messages.

providers.name: Caya
providers.description: Caya (Caya GmbH, Berlin) is a German intelligent document processing (IDP) company whose Document Automation Suite digitizes, classifies, and routes business documents end to end. Its core capabilities are Post Scan (physical mail intake with OCR and automatic classification), Document Extractions (AI-powered structured data extraction), and Document Automations (rule-based routing and distribution into downstream systems). Caya connects to 100+ tools across accounting, ERP, HR, cloud storage, and e-signature, and hosts data in a high-security Frankfurt data center. It is certified and compliant against ISO 27001, GDPR/DSGVO, DORA, GoBD, and German HGB/AO retention rules, with a public Vanta-hosted trust center. Surfaced as an HV Capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CyberGRX
providers.description: CyberGRX is a third-party cyber risk management platform — the Global Risk Exchange (GRX) — that helps organizations assess, monitor, and reduce risk across their vendor and supplier ecosystem. It combines a shared library of standardized vendor risk assessments with analytics for inherent and residual risk, control gaps, and findings. CyberGRX was acquired by ProcessUnity in 2023 and is now delivered as the ProcessUnity Global Risk Exchange. It exposes a versioned REST API (v1, bulk-v1, v2) authenticated with an account API token passed in the Authorization header, including a Bulk API that returns an entire third-party ecosystem — residual risk, control scores, and findings — in a single request, plus first-party Python examples and Go/Splunk connectors.

providers.name: Frame Security
providers.description: Frame Security is an AI-powered human risk management and security awareness platform that defends organizations against human-targeted attacks such as phishing, deepfakes, and social engineering. Frame generates personalized security awareness training in 70+ languages, hyper-realistic email, voice, and video phishing and deepfake simulations built from an organization's own context, employee risk scoring with targeted interventions, automated phishing triage of reported suspicious emails, and cross-platform reporting and integrations. The company is backed by Index Ventures and raised a $50M round in 2026.

providers.name: Second Front Systems
providers.description: Second Front Systems is a public-benefit, venture-backed software company that accelerates government access to emerging technologies for the world's democracies. Its 2F Suite delivers DevSecOps and continuous-accreditation tooling for defense and public-sector software teams: 2F Workshop (integrated security and compliance tooling for accredited development), 2F Game Warden (a fully accredited FedRAMP High and DoD ATO DevSecOps platform that fast-tracks commercial software to classified and unclassified government networks in roughly 90 days), and 2F Frontier (edge deployment to disconnected and denied environments). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It exposes no public developer API; its primary technical surface is the Game Warden platform documentation, a compliance Trust Center, and a broad certification posture (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FIPS 140).

providers.name: Vulcan Technologies
providers.description: Vulcan Technologies builds frontier AI for law and government, headquartered in Austin, Texas and founded in 2025. Its flagship product, Justinian, is a legal AI agent that runs on roughly 157 billion records of American law and policy — including 13+ billion court records, every municipal code, and federal and state statutes, regulations, and active legislative sessions — planning research, drafting work product, and verifying and citing every claim against source. A second product, Trajan, is a government AI concierge for citizen services such as permits, registrations, and license renewals. Vulcan is FedRAMP Ready, runs in AWS GovCloud (US), and serves customers including the Virginia Office of Regulatory Management, the U.S. Department of Education, and South Carolina agencies. The company raised a $10.9M seed round (October 2025) co-led by General Catalyst and Cubit Capital, with participation from Y Combinator, SV Angel, and others. Vulcan is a product/agent company and does not currently publish a public developer API.
